newsitem.title: UK: GM Vauxhall says unhappy with current profits.
newsitem.headline: GM Vauxhall says unhappy with current profits.

text.p: General Motors Corp UK unit Vauxhall said on Tuesday that its pre-tax profits rose to 10 million stg in 1996 from 2.5 million the year earlier.
But chairman and managing director Nick Reilly said, "These returns are clearly not acceptable in the long term."
Reilly said in a statement Vauxhall could "derive some satisfaction from being able to remain profitable in an industry where losses have become the norm."

But he said, "While the UK car market rose by a welcome four percent to just over two million units in the year, over-capacity in the European industry resulted in intensely competitive trading conditions which continued to depress profitability."

"I am optimistic about Vauxhall's potential in the long term," he said, noting the company announced last October a plan to invest 300 million stg "against the trend" in its Ellesmere Port plant on Merseyside, northwest England.
He said the company made further progress in reducing costs in 1996 and was helped by a 14.4 percent rise in output to 278,000 vehicles from 243,000 in 1995.
Vauxhall's parent General Motors on Monday announced a fall in annual net earnings to $786 million in continuing operations from $1.597 billion in 1995.
